newsitem.title: USA: Groups oppose Banc One acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Groups oppose Banc One acquisitions.

text.p: Inner City Press/Community on the Move, a community and consumer group, said Tuesday it was asking the Federal Reserve Board to deny the applications of Banc One Corp. to acquire First USA Inc. and Liberty Bancorp Inc.
Inner City said in a news release that it filed written challenges requesting that a formal hearing be held on the applications.

Matthew Lee, executive director of Inner City, said in a statement that Banc One's bank units in their lending "disproportionately exclude people of colour" and the consumer finance unit Banc One Financial Services "disproportionately targets people of colour for higher than normal interest rate loans."
A spokesman for Columbus, Ohio-headquartered Banc One declined comment, saying the company has not been informed by the Federal Reserve that any protests have been filed.

He also declined comment on Inner City's specific allegations for the same reason. He said protests have been "a normal part of the acquisition business for the past 20 years and we take those in due course."
Banc One is seeking to close both acquisitions in the second quarter of 1997.

It agreed to buy First USA, one of the largest U.S. credit card issuers, for more than $7.3 billion in stock. Liberty Bancorp, an Oklahoma-based bank holding company, agreed to be purchased for $544 million in stock.
Inner City said it was joined in its opposition to the acquisitions by the Delaware Community Reinvestmnt Action Council.
